bias: The broad vol and rates backdrop actually calmed today: MOVE retreated back below the 80 stress threshold it breached on Jul 24 (-4.07% to 76.82), VIX eased a further -1.7%, and the yield curve was essentially flat. Breakevens eased too (T5YIE -5bps, T10YIE -2bps) while oil held its retracement rather than reversing higher - together a modest improvement for the disinflation thesis. But this calm at the index level masks a severe, narrower selloff: SOXX fell -4.40%, DRAM -8.75%, and EWY -6.27% (widening its gap below the 20-day SMA to roughly -8.7%), none of which shows up in VIX or MOVE. Credit also cracked slightly for the first time this cycle - HY OAS widened 9bps to 2.77% after weeks of staying tight - even as single-name proxies were mixed (CACC/ALLY down, COF up). Plumbing data (WALCL/TGA/Reserves) is unchanged, still the Jul 22 H.4.1 vintage, with the next release due Jul 30. Note Asian cash-equity data (KOSPI, SK Hynix, Samsung, Nikkei) is unchanged from the last pull since those markets have been closed since Friday.

counterargs.thesis: Idiosyncratic semis/Korea de-risking diverging from a calming macro vol backdrop, with a first, modest crack in credit
supporting: SOXX -4.40%, DRAM -8.75%, EWY -6.27% - a sharp, sector-specific selloff
HY OAS widened 9bps to 2.77%, its first real move after weeks of tight/flat readings
EWY now trading roughly 8.7% below its 20-day SMA, a wider gap than Jul 24's close
CACC -3.12%, a 5th down session recently, and ALLY -2.39% resuming lower
RRP buffer still near zero ($0.675B) - no cushion restored ahead of the Jul 30 H.4.1
against: MOVE retreated back below 80 (76.82, -4.07%) - the rates-vol stress signal from Jul 24 is easing
VIX eased a further -1.7% - broad equity vol is calm, not spiking
US10Y and the yield curve were essentially flat today - no fresh real-rate pressure
T5YIE/T10YIE breakevens eased rather than rose - disinflation signal intact
COF +1.44% - not all credit proxies confirm the CACC/ALLY softness
counterargs.read: This reads as a narrow, sector-specific drawdown in semis and Korea rather than a broad macro risk-off event - the index-level vol gauges (VIX, MOVE) both eased and the curve was flat, which is inconsistent with a systemic liquidity or rates shock. The HY OAS widening is the one genuine new crack worth watching, since credit had been the calm anchor through the Jul 22-24 turbulence; if it continues to widen alongside further semis/Korea weakness, that would upgrade this from idiosyncratic to systemic. For now, treat SOXX/DRAM/EWY weakness as name/sector-specific and watch HY OAS and the Jul 30 H.4.1 print as the next confirming or disconfirming data points.
